caption: The drawing shows a detailed design of a looking-glass shelf clock labeled as the "Chauncey Jerome Pattern" from circa 1830-1835, rendered in pencil on an off-white or light tan background. The left side presents the "Front Elevation," featuring a rectangular clock structure divided into three sections: the top section displays an ornamental carving of an eagle with outspread wings, the middle section is labeled "MIRROR," and the bottom section is a plain rectangular panel. Flanking the three sections on each side are decorative vertical strips with detailed patterns. The overall height is recorded as 39 7/8 inches, and the width as 16 5/8 inches. On the right, the "Side Elevation" shows the profile view of the clock, which is 5 3/8 inches deep, including the side detailing. Above the drawings, the text notes the name, pattern, era, and includes a scale bar. The drawing is technical in nature, with straight, neat lines and no shading or colors except for the pencil's gray tone.
title: Shelf Clock
